metadata.title: Global Agricultural Subsidies, Grants & Financial Incentive Database
metadata.pilotJurisdiction: California (CDFA / CARB / CEC / USDA California State Office)

programs.name: CDFA State Water Efficiency and Enhancement Program (SWEEP)
programs.agency: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) - OEFI
programs.subsidyRate: 100% Grant Funding (No Grower Match Required)
programs.matchRequirement: 0% (Zero grower matching funds required; matching funds optional for higher merit points)
programs.disbursementType: Advance Payment (up to 25% for eligible applicants) + Quarterly Progress Invoicing
programs.deadline: Continuous Batching / Next Solicitation Window Closes Q4 2026
programs.selectionMethod: Competitive Merit Scoring & Point-Ranked Technical Review
targetEquipment: Solar PV arrays dedicated to powering irrigation booster & well pumps
Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) installation on agricultural pumps
Soil moisture telemetry probes (Capacitance, TDR, C-Probe) & weather stations
Conversion from flood/furrow to micro-drip & low-pressure micro-sprinklers
Automated irrigation line valves, flow meters, and telemetry controllers
ineligibleItems: General operational labor, tractor fuel, and maintenance overhead
Repair or maintenance of existing non-upgraded equipment
Expenses incurred prior to formal execution of the CDFA grant agreement
Leased equipment where ownership does not transfer to the agricultural producer
qualificationCriteria: Commercial agricultural operations on land located within California
Must demonstrate verifiable water savings AND greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions
Must possess legal water rights or active agricultural groundwater well metering
Leased land requires signed Landowner Consent and minimum remaining lease term
documentChecklist: Certified Pump Efficiency Test Report (completed within the last 24 months by PG&E/SCE/APEP accredited tester)
CDFA SWEEP Water Savings & GHG Calculator Output Spreadsheet (official quantification tool)
Three (3) Itemized Vendor Quotes for all proposed equipment/solar packages (valid within 90 days)
Farm Layout Map & APN Parcel Diagram indicating pump, sensor, and pipeline locations
California Payee Data Record (STD 204) & Federal IRS Form W-9
Landowner Consent Form (mandatory if farm property is leased)
programs.summary: California's premier water and clean energy grant covering up to $200,000 at 100% funding to upgrade irrigation pumps to solar/VFD and install real-time soil moisture telemetry.
programs.deepGuide: Step 1: Obtain a certified pump efficiency test from an electric utility (PG&E/SCE). Step 2: Model water and GHG reduction using the CDFA calculator. Step 3: Secure 3 vendor bids. Step 4: Submit via CDFA AmpliFund portal.

applicationWindow.cycleFrequency: 연 1회 가을 정기 공모 (Annual Fall Solicitation)

programs.name: CDFA Healthy Soils Program (HSP) Incentives
programs.agency: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) - OEFI
programs.subsidyRate: Fixed Acreage Payment Rates (Covers 80% - 100% of Practice Implementation)
programs.matchRequirement: 0% (Zero match required; flat payment rates per acre/ton)
programs.disbursementType: Annual Practice Verification & Flat-Rate Reimbursement
programs.deadline: First-Come, First-Served Rolling Review until Funding Cap Exhausted
programs.selectionMethod: First-Come, First-Served for Eligible Applications meeting minimum threshold
targetEquipment: Commercial compost application (on-farm and purchased certified organic compost)
Cover cropping seed blends (legume, cereal, brassica mixtures)
Whole orchard recycling (chipping and incorporating old fruit/nut trees into soil)
Hedgerow planting, windbreak establishment, and pollinator strips
Reduced tillage, conservation tillage, and no-till drill implementation
ineligibleItems: Continuation of soil practices already implemented prior to grant award
Commercial synthetic chemical fertilizers and synthetic pesticides
Capital purchase of tractors, heavy earthmoving machinery, or vehicles
Soil amendments not listed on CDFA approved practice guidelines
qualificationCriteria: California agricultural operations, croplands, orchards, vineyards, and rangelands
Producers must commit to maintaining practice for full 3-year agreement period
Prior receipt of HSP funding on the exact same field parcel is disqualified
Must utilize CDFA-COMET-Planner to quantify GHG sequestration
documentChecklist: CDFA HSP COMET-Planner GHG Quantification Report
Field Boundary Map with APN parcel numbers and GPS coordinates
Baseline Soil Organic Matter (SOM) Test Report (sampled within last 12 months)
Compost Certificate of Analysis (verifying C:N ratio and heavy metal compliance)
Completed California Payee Data Record (STD 204)
programs.summary: Direct incentive grants up to $100,000 providing flat per-acre cash payments to California farmers for compost application, cover cropping, and whole orchard recycling.
programs.deepGuide: Step 1: Map fields and calculate baseline soil organic matter. Step 2: Run COMET-Planner to estimate carbon benefits. Step 3: Submit early as applications are processed first-come, first-served.

applicationWindow.deadlineDisplay: 상시 선착순 접수 (예산 소진 시 조기 마감)

programs.name: California Food Production Investment Program (FPIP) - CEA & Ag Processing
programs.agency: California Energy Commission (CEC) & CDFA
programs.subsidyRate: Up to 65% of Total Eligible Equipment & Installation Costs
programs.matchRequirement: 35% Applicant Match (Cash or certified commercial loan financing)
programs.disbursementType: Milestone Progress Reimbursement (with 10% retention until commissioning)
programs.deadline: Annual Solicitation Cycle (Cut-off Window: Late 2026)
programs.selectionMethod: Competitive Technical Scoring & Benefit-Cost Ratio Evaluation
targetEquipment: Advanced horticultural LED luminaires replacing HPS/HID in CEA facilities
Natural refrigerant industrial refrigeration systems (CO2 transcritical / NH3)
Industrial heat pumps for greenhouse root zone heating & drying facilities
Automated dual thermal climate screens and triple-layer greenhouse envelopes
Flue gas heat recovery, waste heat economizers, and microgrid solar PV
ineligibleItems: Production equipment unrelated to energy efficiency or GHG reduction
Facility land acquisition or construction of shell buildings
Research and development unproven technologies without field readiness
Contingency allowances and indirect administrative overhead exceeding 10%
qualificationCriteria: Food production, cold storage, packaging, or commercial CEA greenhouse facilities located in California
Facility must pay into the California Climate Investments (GGRF) fund
Project must demonstrate a minimum simple payback reduction of at least 30%
Must provide baseline 12 months of utility electricity and natural gas bills
documentChecklist: Professional Engineering (PE) Certified Energy & GHG Audit
12 Consecutive Months of Utility Electric & Gas Invoices with Interval Meter Data
Equipment Vendor Technical Cut Sheets & Detailed Engineering Design Drawings
Proof of 35% Matching Funds (Bank Statement, Credit Line, or Financing Approval)
California CEQA Environmental Compliance Documentation
programs.summary: Massive state grant providing up to $5,000,000 (covering 65% of costs) for California CEA greenhouses and food packing facilities upgrading to advanced LED, heat pumps, and dual thermal screens.
programs.deepGuide: Requires a formal PE energy audit. Highly competitive. Focus heavily on verified therms and kWh saved per dollar of grant requested.

applicationWindow.cycleFrequency: 연 1회 대규모 설비 경쟁 공모 (Annual Competitive)
applicationWindow.submissionPortal: California Energy Commission Energy Commission e-Grant Portal

programs.name: CDFA Alternative Manure Management Program (AMMP)
programs.agency: California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) - OEFI
programs.subsidyRate: 100% of Eligible Project Costs (Up to Grant Limit)
programs.matchRequirement: 0% (No matching funds required; in-kind support optional)
programs.disbursementType: Advance Payment (up to 25%) + Invoiced Milestone Reimbursements
programs.deadline: Annual Solicitation Batch (Next Deadline: Fall 2026)
programs.selectionMethod: Competitive Technical Scoring based on Greenhouse Gas Abatement Cost-Effectiveness
targetEquipment: Mechanical solid separators (screw press, rotary drum, weeping wall systems)
Compost bedded pack barns and aerated static pile composting systems
Scrape manure collection conversion retrofits replacing flush lagoon systems
Solar drying bays and manure solid processing machinery
ineligibleItems: Anaerobic digester installations (covered separately under DDRDP program)
Feed additives and animal nutrition supplements
General farm machinery not directly related to manure solids separation
Costs incurred prior to project contract execution
qualificationCriteria: Commercial dairy and livestock operations located in California
Currently utilizing a flush manure lagoon or anaerobic storage system
Must implement a non-digester manure management practice that reduces methane
Must maintain the practice for a minimum operating life of 5 years
documentChecklist: CDFA AMMP GHG Quantification Calculator Output (official CARB tool)
Regional Water Quality Control Board Waste Discharge Requirement (WDR) Permit
Site Engineering Layout & Process Flow Schematics
Written Equipment Vendor Quotes for all mechanical separators and electrical hookups
California Payee Data Record (STD 204)
programs.summary: Offers up to $750,000 at 100% state grant funding for California dairies and livestock farms converting to solid separators and compost bedded pack systems to eliminate lagoon methane emissions.
programs.deepGuide: Ensure coordination with your local Regional Water Quality Control Board prior to submission. Scoring hinges on metric tons of CO2e reduced.

programs.name: California Specialty Crop Block Grant Program (SCBGP)
programs.agency: CDFA / USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS)
programs.subsidyRate: 100% Non-Repayable Project Grant
programs.matchRequirement: 0% Mandatory Match (Matching funds strongly encouraged and scored favorably)
programs.disbursementType: Quarterly Cost Reimbursement based on milestone deliverables
programs.deadline: Two-Phase Annual Cycle: Concept Proposal Q4 2026 / Full Proposal Q1 2027
programs.selectionMethod: Two-Stage Competitive Review (Technical Review Committee & CDFA Panel)
targetEquipment: Precision smart farm sensor networks for specialty fruit, nut, and vegetable crops
CEA greenhouse pest biological control automation and drone dispersal systems
Post-harvest shelf-life extension and sorting technology for California specialty crops
Horticultural AI diagnostic vision hardware and automated yield forecasting tools
ineligibleItems: Projects benefiting a single private commercial farm without broader industry benefit
Direct production subsidies or operating costs of staple commodity crops (wheat, corn, cotton)
General agricultural real estate or permanent land acquisition
Lobbying or political activities
qualificationCriteria: California non-profits, agricultural trade associations, university researchers, and collaborative grower groups
Project must solely benefit California specialty crops (fruits, vegetables, tree nuts, dried fruits, horticulture, nursery, and greenhouse floriculture)
Must generate publicly accessible data and measurable industry-wide benefits
Must complete all deliverables within a strict 3-year performance period
documentChecklist: Concept Proposal & Scope of Work Narrative
Letters of Support from California Specialty Crop Grower Associations (minimum 3)
Detailed Itemized 3-Year Budget Spreadsheet with Justification Narrative
Key Personnel Resumes and Project Manager Qualifications
Data Sharing and Public Accessibility Plan
programs.summary: State-administered federal grant funding up to $500,000 for innovative smart agriculture, pest control robotics, and post-harvest technology benefiting California specialty crop growers.
programs.deepGuide: Phase 1 requires a concise Concept Proposal. Projects that partner with grower cooperatives or demonstrate clear industry-wide dissemination score highest.

applicationWindow.cycleFrequency: 연 1회 정기 공모 (Annual Speciality Crop Cycle)

programs.name: USDA NRCS California EQIP (Specialty Crop & High Tunnel Initiative)
programs.agency: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (California State Office, Davis CA)
programs.subsidyRate: 50% - 75% Standard (Up to 90% for Historically Underserved / Beginning Farmers)
programs.maxAmount: $450,000 per Farm Bill lifecycle (Up to $10,000/acre for high tunnels)
programs.matchRequirement: 10% - 50% Producer Match depending on producer classification
programs.disbursementType: Flat-Rate Practice Reimbursement upon NRCS Field Inspection & Verification
programs.deadline: Continuous Intake / Annual State Ranking Cut-Offs (November & March)
programs.selectionMethod: NRCS Conservation Assessment Ranking Tool (CART) Merit Score
targetEquipment: Commercial High Tunnels (Hoop Houses, Practice Code 325) for season extension
Micro-irrigation retrofits (Practice Code 441) including drip tubing & filtration
Irrigation Water Management (IWM Practice 449) automated soil moisture logging
Agricultural stationary combustion engine replacement (CARB Tier 4 clean diesel/electric)
Cover crop seed establishment and conservation crop rotation
ineligibleItems: Heated commercial permanent glasshouses (only unheated high tunnels eligible under Practice 325)
Equipment purchased or installed prior to contract obligation and NRCS approval
General operational costs, commercial seed purchases for cash crop harvest
Producers with Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) exceeding $900,000 (unless granted waiver)
qualificationCriteria: Agricultural producers holding an established USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Farm and Tract Number
Compliance with USDA Highly Erodible Land and Wetland Conservation (AD-1026)
Average Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) below $900,000 for the prior 3 tax years
Must hold control of the land (deed or written lease spanning the practice lifespan)
documentChecklist: USDA FSA Farm and Tract Registration (Form AD-2047)
Highly Erodible Land Conservation and Wetland Certification (Form AD-1026)
Average Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) Certification Form (CCC-941)
NRCS Conservation Plan developed with your local District Conservationist
High Tunnel or Irrigation System Engineering Quotes and Site Map
programs.summary: Federal cost-share funding 75% to 90% of the cost to construct commercial high tunnels and precision drip irrigation across California's valleys, with special priority for beginning growers.
programs.deepGuide: Step 1: Visit your local USDA Service Center in your California county to get a Farm/Tract number. Step 2: Request an on-site visit from an NRCS conservationist. Step 3: Rank your application in the CART tool.

applicationWindow.cycleFrequency: 연중 상시 접수 후 분기별 랭킹 평가 (Quarterly Ranking Batches)
applicationWindow.submissionPortal: USDA Farmers.gov / Local NRCS Service Center

programs.name: USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) Clean Energy Grants
programs.agency: USDA Rural Development (National & California State Office)
programs.subsidyRate: Up to 50% Non-Repayable Capital Grant (IRA Clean Energy Allocation)
programs.maxAmount: Renewables: Up to $1,000,000 | Energy Efficiency: Up to $500,000
programs.matchRequirement: 50% Applicant Match (Can combine with 30% Federal Investment Tax Credit for ~80% total recovery!)
programs.disbursementType: Post-Installation Reimbursement upon Certified Commissioning & Utility Interconnection
programs.deadline: Quarterly Continuous Batching (March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31)
programs.selectionMethod: Point-Ranked Priority Scoring (Scoring based on % energy generated/saved and payback)
targetEquipment: Agricultural rooftop, carport, and ground-mount Solar PV installations
Geothermal and industrial ground/air-source heat pumps for commercial greenhouses
Commercial horticultural LED retrofits replacing high-pressure sodium fixtures
Dual thermal shade screens, motorized insulated louvers, and curtain walls
High-efficiency ventilation fans, VFD motors, and refrigeration compressor retrofits
ineligibleItems: Residential solar or heating installations not dedicated to commercial agriculture
Agricultural operations earning less than 50% of gross revenue from farming unless located in designated rural areas
Equipment ordered or contracted prior to environmental review (NEPA) clearance
Used or refurbished equipment lacking original manufacturer warranties
qualificationCriteria: Agricultural producers with ≥50% of gross annual income derived from farming operations (no rural area restriction for producers)
Rural small businesses located in eligible non-metro areas with population < 50,000
Must be registered in the federal System for Award Management (SAM.gov) with an active UEI number
Projects over $200,000 require an independent certified Technical Report or Energy Audit
documentChecklist: Active SAM.gov Registration & Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
Independent Certified Energy Audit (for projects > $200,000) or Energy Assessment (for < $200,000)
Form RD 4280-3A or 4280-3B (USDA REAP Application)
Prior 3 Years Federal Tax Returns documenting agricultural gross income ratio
Utility Interconnection Agreement & 12 Months Electric Billing History
programs.summary: Flagship federal program covering 50% of capital costs for solar arrays, heat pumps, and LED retrofits. When stacked with the 30% IRS Section 48 ITC tax credit, California growers recover up to 80% of total costs!
programs.deepGuide: Ensure you get your SAM.gov UEI early as verification can take 3-4 weeks. Pair REAP with the 30% federal ITC tax credit and California net-metering rules for rapid ROI under 2.5 years.

programs.name: Bundesprogramm Energieeffizienz in Landwirtschaft und Gartenbau
programs.agency: Bundesanstalt für Landwirtschaft und Ernährung (BLE) / BMEL
programs.subsidyRate: 30% - 40% of Total Investment Cost
programs.maxAmount: €600,000 per project (€1.2M for combined consortium measures)
programs.matchRequirement: 60% - 70% Enterprise Match (Own equity or commercial bank loan)
programs.disbursementType: Progress Reimbursement based on verified invoices and consultant certification
programs.deadline: Rolling Intake / Continuous Federal Budget Window
programs.selectionMethod: First-Come, First-Served for verified applications meeting ≥20% CO2 savings threshold
targetEquipment: High-performance thermal climate screens (Energieschirme: Svensson, Bonar, Phormium)
Industrial horticultural LED lighting fixtures replacing high-pressure sodium
Insulating greenhouse glazing retrofits (Doppelstegplatten, diffuse isolierglas)
Flue gas heat recovery condensers, buffer tanks, and latent heat exchangers
ineligibleItems: Greenhouse construction or expansion without proven energy savings
Measures ordered or commenced prior to official Zuwendungsbescheid approval
Second-hand or used horticultural machinery
General operational expenditure and production consumables
qualificationCriteria: Commercial horticultural and agricultural enterprises located in Germany
Minimum 20% certified CO2/energy savings verified by an accredited energy consultant (Energieberater)
Enterprise must fulfill EU SME (KMU) definition or agricultural enterprise status
Must operate existing greenhouse facilities for at least 3 years
documentChecklist: Energieberatungsbericht (Certified Energy Concept prepared by an accredited consultant)
CO2-Minderungsberechnung (Official BLE carbon reduction calculation sheet)
Two to three detailed commercial quotes from certified horticultural builders
Commercial Register Excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug / Gewerbeanmeldung)
De-minimis declaration and KMU self-assessment declaration
programs.summary: Germany's flagship greenhouse modernization grant covering up to 40% of capital costs for thermal screens, LED conversion, and greenhouse insulation with €600,000 grant ceiling.
programs.deepGuide: Must hire an accredited Energieberater before purchasing any equipment. The grant contract must be formally issued by BLE before placing purchase orders.

programs.name: Agrarinvestitionsförderungsprogramm (AFP) Nordrhein-Westfalen
programs.agency: Landwirtschaftskammer Nordrhein-Westfalen (LWK NRW)
programs.subsidyRate: 20% - 40% of Eligible Capital Investment
programs.matchRequirement: 60% - 80% Farm Equity or Rentenbank Agricultural Loan
programs.disbursementType: Milestone-based inspection and construction draws
programs.deadline: Bi-Annual Cut-Off Windows (Spring / Autumn Selection Rounds)
programs.selectionMethod: Competitive Ranking based on environmental and animal welfare indicators
targetEquipment: New modern Venlo glasshouse construction with integrated energy conservation
Closed-loop nutrient recirculation systems with UV/Ozone disinfection
Automated climate computers and precision irrigation fertigation rigs
Rainwater collection holding basins, buffer reservoirs, and pumping stations
ineligibleItems: Purchase of production rights, quotas, and agricultural land
Simple replacement investments without technological innovation
Machinery that does not exceed standard legal environmental baselines
Projects commenced prior to written funding pre-approval
qualificationCriteria: Horticultural businesses in NRW (Straelen / Niederrhein) demonstrating long-term economic viability
Manager must possess certified vocational agricultural qualifications (Gärtnermeister / Agraringenieur)
Minimum 25% farm income generated from production
Must submit a comprehensive agricultural investment and business plan
documentChecklist: Wirtschaftlichkeitsberechnung (3-Year Business Viability Forecast)
Approved Building Permit (Baugenehmigung) and Water District Drainage Permits
Itemized Construction Cost Estimate formatted to DIN 276 standards
Proof of Vocational Qualification (Meisterbrief / Diplom)
Financing Confirmation Letter from Commercial Bank or Rentenbank
programs.summary: Premier structural modernization grant in Germany's largest horticultural cluster (Straelen / Niederrhein) supporting new glasshouses, closed-loop hydroponics, and climate computers up to €2,000,000.
programs.deepGuide: Ensure building permits are fully granted prior to the application deadline. The scoring rubric gives heavy preference to closed-loop water recirculation.

programs.name: GAP Junglandwirte-Einkommensunterstützung & Niederlassungsprämie
programs.agency: Landwirtschaftskammer / EU CAP
programs.subsidyType: Direct Income Top-Up & Capital Settlement Grant
programs.subsidyRate: Fixed Acreage Top-Up + Up to €70,000 Settlement Bonus
programs.matchRequirement: 0% (Direct non-repayable income injection and settlement capital)
programs.disbursementType: Annual Single Area Payment (Direktzahlung) + Staged Settlement Tranches
programs.deadline: Annual Single Application Window (May 15 Cut-off)
programs.selectionMethod: Non-Competitive Entitlement for all eligible applicants meeting qualification
targetEquipment: Farm acquisition, greenhouse leasehold, and initial working capital
Digital crop steering sensors, mobile telemetry, and diagnostic meters
First-time horticultural machinery and nursery establishment supplies
Enterprise software, digital accounting, and farm ERP systems
ineligibleItems: Applicants reaching age 40 prior to the year of establishment
Businesses where young farmer holds less than 50% voting control
Establishments older than 5 years at time of first application
qualificationCriteria: Business manager under 40 years of age established as head of holding within past 5 years
Certified vocational education in agriculture or horticulture (Berufsabschluss / Meister / Studium)
Must hold effective and long-term financial/managerial control of the agricultural enterprise
Registered farm operation with active Betriebsnummer
documentChecklist: Gemeinsamer Antrag (Annual Single Application submitted via ANDI/LEA/DIANA)
Proof of Vocational Qualification (Meisterprüfungszeugnis / Hochschulabschluss)
Company Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) verifying majority voting control
Commercial Farm Registration (Betriebsnummernachweis)
Business Takeover or Establishment Agreement (Übergabevertrag)
programs.summary: Special young farmer bonus providing a direct €70,000 cash grant plus €134/ha/year for 5 years to support newly qualified Gärtnermeister and agricultural founders.
programs.deepGuide: Must submit together with your state's Gemeinsamer Antrag before May 15. Ensure company bylaws explicitly show the young farmer holds effective executive control.

applicationWindow.cycleFrequency: 매년 봄 GAP 통합신청 (Annual Direct Payment Window)

programs.name: 스마트팜 ICT 융복합 확산사업 (Smart Farm ICT Convergence)
programs.agency: 농림축산식품부 (MAFRA) / 농어촌공사 / 지자체 농업기술센터
programs.maxAmount: 온실 ha당 최대 2억 ~ 5억 원 지원 한도
programs.matchRequirement: 자부담 10% ~ 20% (융자 30% 별도 지원 가능)
programs.disbursementType: 감리 및 현장 검수 완료 후 시공업체 직접 지급 (e나라도움 시스템)
programs.deadline: 매년 1~2월 정기 공모 및 지자체별 잔여예산 하반기 2차 접수
programs.selectionMethod: 전문가 현장 실사 및 ICT 도입 적격성 심사 평가
targetEquipment: 온실 내외부 복합 기상센서 (일사량, 온습도, 풍향풍속, CO2)
국가 표준 규격 복합환경제어기 (Complex Climate Computer)
정밀 자동 양액공급기 및 배액 수질 계측기
원격 모바일 모니터링 CCTV 및 천측창 전동 구동기 모터
ineligibleItems: 스마트팜 국가 표준(KS) 규격 미인증 비표준 장비
단순 온실 골조 및 비닐 교체 등 하드웨어 일반 소모품
사업 승인 전 사전 구매 또는 선시공된 자재
농가 일상 운영비, 비료, 종자 등 영농 자재
qualificationCriteria: 시설원예(채소·화훼) 재배 농업인 또는 농업회사법인
국립농산물품질관리원 농업경영체 등록 완료 농가 (필수)
ICT 장비를 설치할 수 있는 연동 또는 단동 내재해형 규격 온실 보유 농가
스마트팜 전문 교육 20시간 이상 이수 농가 가점 부여
documentChecklist: 스마트팜 ICT 융복합 사업 신청서 및 사업계획서
농업경영체 등록확인서 (최근 1개월 이내 발급)
표준 ICT 장비 규격서 및 공인 시공업체 비교 견적서 2부
온실 부지 토지대장 및 건축물대장 (임차 시 5년 이상 임대차계약서)
스마트팜 농업인 교육 이수증 사본
programs.summary: 한국 농식품부의 대표 스마트팜 사업으로 복합환경제어기, 센서, 자동 양액기 등 ICT 설비비의 50~70%를 정부와 지자체가 직접 지원.
programs.deepGuide: 스마트팜코리아(smartfarmkorea.net) 사전 가입 필수. KS 표준 인증 장비를 채택해야 하며, 관할 시군 농업기술센터에 방문 또는 e나라도움으로 접수.

applicationWindow.cycleFrequency: 연 1회 시군구 농정부서 공모 (Annual Municipal Call)

programs.name: 농업에너지이용효율화사업 (Agri-Energy Efficiency Improvement)
programs.agency: 농림축산식품부 / 한국농어촌공사 / 지자체
programs.subsidyRate: 50% 무상 보조 (국비 20% + 지방비 30% + 융자 30% + 자부담 20%)
programs.matchRequirement: 자부담 20% (정책 융자 30% 지원 가능)
programs.disbursementType: 한국농어촌공사 감리 승인 후 준공 검사 완료 시 시공업체 직접 지급
programs.deadline: 매년 7~9월 익년도 사업 사전 수요조사 및 1월 본신청
programs.selectionMethod: 난방 에너지 절감률 산출 모델 및 농가 평가 기준표 심사
targetEquipment: 알루미늄 단열 스크린 및 다겹보온커튼 개폐 설비
지열 히트펌프 및 공기열 히트펌프 냉난방 시스템

Native tree and shrub plantings around irrigation reservoirs and greenhouses

programs.portalName: Valley Air District Online Grant Portal
programs.summary: San Joaquin Valley incentive providing $600-$750/acre (up to $60,000 per grower) to chip and recycle whole orchards into the soil rather than open-burning, dramatically increasing soil water retention.
programs.deepGuide: Step 1: Apply to SJVAPCD BEFORE pulling trees. Step 2: Receive Voucher. Step 3: Contractor chips and incorporates wood into soil. Step 4: Submit invoice for prompt check payment.

programs.name: CDFA Water Efficiency Technical Assistance (WETA)
programs.agency: CDFA Office of Environmental Farming & University of California Cooperative Extension (UCCE)
programs.subsidyType: 100% Free Specialized Technical Service & Engineering Audit
programs.subsidyRate: 100% Free Service ($10,000+ Market Value per Irrigation Audit)
programs.maxAmount: Free Engineering Services & Pump Test Vouchers (No Cash Cap)
programs.matchRequirement: 0% (Zero grower cost)
programs.disbursementType: Direct Service Provision by University / Resource Conservation District Engineers
programs.deadline: Continuous Enrollment / First-Come Basis
programs.selectionMethod: Non-competitive; Available to all California agricultural growers with irrigation pumps
targetEquipment: Free Mobile Irrigation Lab (MIL) distribution uniformity and pressure tests
Free certified agricultural pump efficiency testing and cavitation diagnostics
Free technical design support for CDFA SWEEP and USDA EQIP grant applications
Free soil moisture sensor calibration and irrigation scheduling workshops
ineligibleItems: Direct cash grants to purchase hardware (hardware funded separately via SWEEP)
Technical assistance for residential gardens or golf courses
qualificationCriteria: Active California commercial farmer, greenhouse operator, or rancher
Priority service scheduling for socially disadvantaged farmers, small acreage, and language-minority growers
Grower agrees to grant field access to UCCE/RCD irrigation specialists
documentChecklist: Simple online grower intake form (Location, acreage, crop type)
Recent electric or diesel utility bill showing agricultural pump meter number
General farm parcel map indicating pump and main pipeline locations
programs.summary: 100% free technical assistance providing certified irrigation pump testing, mobile irrigation uniformity audits, and one-on-one engineering support to prepare winning CDFA SWEEP applications.
programs.deepGuide: Step 1: Sign up with your local UCCE or RCD technical partner. Step 2: Irrigation specialist visits farm to test pump and system uniformity. Step 3: Receive official report to attach to your SWEEP grant.

programs.name: California Energy Commission (CEC) EPIC: Ag Microgrids & CEA Demand Flexibility
programs.agency: California Energy Commission (CEC) - Energy Research and Development Division
programs.subsidyType: Competitive R&D and Commercial Demonstration Grant
programs.subsidyRate: 50% - 80% Cost-Share Grant Funding
programs.maxAmount: $3,000,000 per commercial CEA / ag processing facility
programs.matchRequirement: 20% - 50% non-state matching funds (cash or verified private capital)
programs.disbursementType: Milestone-Based Progress Reimbursement Invoicing
programs.deadline: 2026-12-01 Solicitation Window
programs.selectionMethod: Rigorous Competitive Scoring based on Grid Resiliency, Peak Shifting (kW), and GHG Reduction
targetEquipment: Commercial greenhouse Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS, 500 kWh - 4 MWh)
Chilled water and hot water Thermal Energy Storage (TES) buffer tanks for CEA climate control
Automated Demand Response (AutoDR) telemetry integrating with California CAISO wholesale markets
Agri-voltaic microgrid controllers coordinating rooftop/ground solar PV with greenhouse LED lighting
ineligibleItems: Standard non-flexible LED fixtures without smart dimming / automated curtailment capability
Diesel or fossil-fueled emergency generators
Projects that do not deliver measurable electric load shifting during 4 PM - 9 PM grid peak hours
qualificationCriteria: Commercial greenhouses, vertical farms, or post-harvest cold storage located in IOU electric territory (PG&E, SCE, SDG&E)
Must demonstrate at least 20% peak grid demand reduction during summer peak events
Must provide letter of support from electric utility confirming grid interconnection viability
Must share anonymized interval energy performance data with CEC research repository
documentChecklist: Detailed Microgrid / BESS Electrical Single-Line Diagram (SLD) signed by CA Professional Engineer (PE)
12 Months of 15-minute interval Green Button utility electric consumption data
Comprehensive match funding commitment letters and corporate financial statements
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) compliance self-certification
Subcontractor statements of work and detailed equipment cost breakdown tables
programs.portalName: CEC Energy Commission Agreement Management System (ECAMS)
programs.summary: Large-scale California grant providing $500k-$3M to equip commercial greenhouses and CEA facilities with battery storage, thermal buffers, and microgrid controllers to eliminate peak electricity charges.
programs.deepGuide: Step 1: Download 15-minute Green Button energy data. Step 2: Work with storage engineering vendor for single-line diagram. Step 3: Secure match letters. Step 4: Submit via ECAMS portal.
